title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #28476 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #28476

**Parent issue:** #28476 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #28476 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#28476 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 28476 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #28476, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 28476 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 28476 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 28476 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 28476 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/28476" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #28476 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #28476.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

<!-- aidevops:generator=large-file-simplification-gate cited_file=.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh threshold=2000 -->

## What
Simplify `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`. It is currently 2047 lines, over the 2000-line limit. Split it into smaller, focused modules.

title: feat: schedule once recheck/snooze policy and failure advisories for follow-up checks
body:
## What

`aidevops schedule once` runs one fresh worker at a due time. Follow-up checks ("recheck tomorrow, then again until it lands") need more than that: when the criteria are not met yet, they should snooze and try again later within bounds, close themselves when the criteria are met, and tell the operator when they give up. Today a follow-up that is not ready can only fail or succeed once, and a failure is visible only through `aidevops schedule status`.

Seen this session: a 24-hour hosting-incident recheck and an upstream PR review check both needed "check, and if not ready, check again later".

## Change

- `deferred-job-helper.sh once`: `--recheck-every DURATION` (min 5m), `--max-checks N` (default 6, max 100), `--until ISO-UTC`. Stored as a `recheck` object on the job. Refused for manual `--issue` dispatch, which cannot report a snooze.

title: t19176: fix(pulse): release stale assignees from status:available auto-dispatch issues
body:
## Task


Add a proactive normalization pass that releases stale assignees from open `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issues. "Stale" means the assignee has no active claim: their worker attempt ended, or the issue was reopened after they were assigned. The issue then becomes unassigned and any runner can take it. Policy (maintainer, 2026-11-19): an assignee who is no longer working toward a fix should give up the assignment, so other runners can try.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add a proactive normalization pass that releases stale assignees from open `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issues. "Stale" means the assignee has no active claim: their worker attempt ended, or the issue was reopened after they were assigned. The issue then becomes unassigned and any runner can take it. Policy (maintainer, 2026-11-19): an assignee who is no longer working toward a fix should give up the assignment, so other runners can try.

## Why

Observed on #36027. The Oct 30 worker released its claim (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete`) and the issue was closed. It was reopened twice (Nov 8, Nov 16) with `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`, but `alex-solovyev` stayed assigned until a maintainer removed the assignment by hand on Nov 19.

No current path releases that assignment:

- `_normalize_unassign_stale` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:557`) only looks at issues with `status:queued` or `status:in-progress` (filter at line ~610).
- GH#39030 (`_pir_prior_lifecycle_assignees`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:1278`) only runs inside `_action_rsd_single`, which heals open + `status:done`. Manual reopens, large-file gate reopens (`_large_file_gate_reopen_debt_issue`) and consolidation reopens never pass through it.
- The reactive Layer-6 recovery (`_is_stale_assignment`, `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:1305`) only runs when dispatch reaches the candidate. `_dispatch_order_claim_state_candidates` (GH#38333) moves every candidate with a non-passive assignee behind all fresh work. In a deep backlog those candidates are never reached, so they are never recovered.

The result: on every runner except the assignee's own, the issue waits indefinitely.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`: add `_normalize_unassign_available_stale <runner_user> <repos_json> <now_epoch> <dedup_helper>`. Use `_normalize_unassign_stale` as the pattern: the same repo rotation (`_normalize_rotated_slugs` / `_normalize_mark_repo_started`), the same `repo_allows_pulse_write_actions` gate and the same `_normalize_repo_listing` reuse.
  - Candidates are open issues with `status:available` and `auto-dispatch`, at least one assignee, none of `status:queued|in-progress|in-review|claimed`, no hold label (`hold-for-review`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `parent-task`, `persistent`, `no-auto-dispatch`), not `origin:interactive` without `auto-dispatch`, and `updatedAt` older than `STALE_REASSIGN_UPDATED_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` (default 600).
  - Fast path: when `_pir_prior_lifecycle_assignees` returns logins (assigned before the latest reopen), remove exactly those logins with `--remove-assignee`. Log `released prior-lifecycle assignees`.
  - Otherwise call the existing guard `"$dedup_helper" is-assigned <issue> <slug> <runner_user>`. Its `_is_stale_assignment` already provides positive-proof, fail-closed cross-runner recovery and the audit comment. Do not reimplement staleness rules.
  - Limit the pass to `AIDEVOPS_AVAILABLE_STALE_ASSIGNEE_CAP` issues per cycle (default 5) to protect the GitHub API budget. On any read failure, make no mutation.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh`: add `unassign_available_stale` to `_NORMALIZE_PASSES` after `unassign_stale`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`: add the dispatch `case` for the new pass next to `unassign_stale)` (around line 1110). Add a Pass 2c line to the comment block at the top of `normalize_active_issue_assignments`.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`: update the existing pass-order assertion (`EXPECTED_PASS_LOG`, around line 729) to include the new pass. Do not add new test infrastructure.
- Do NOT edit `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`. #36027 is splitting that file, and this fix must not depend on dispatch ordering.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An open `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issue whose assignee was assigned before the latest reopen loses that assignee within one normalization cycle. An assignee added at or after the reopen is kept.
- [ ] An assignee with no reopen evidence is released only when `is-assigned` stale recovery proves staleness. An active worker, a recent dispatch claim, a recent branch push, or an API failure leaves the assignment unchanged.
- [ ] Issues with active status labels, hold labels, or an `origin:interactive` claim without `auto-dispatch` are never touched.
- [ ] No more than the configured cap of issues is processed per cycle. ShellCheck is clean on every edited file.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-rotation.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reassign-self-normalization.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`
- Ad hoc: run the real `_normalize_unassign_available_stale` with stubbed `gh` and a stubbed `dedup_helper` against fixture rows (reopen after assignment, assignment after reopen, active label, hold label, API failure).
- After deploy, `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows `released prior-lifecycle assignees` or stale-recovery lines for available issues, and fewer `dispatch_candidate_claimed_demoted` entries.

</details>

title: route-upstream issues all share one fixed title, so distinct findings look like duplicates
body:
## Problem

`cmd_route_upstream` in `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` (around line 1124) creates every routed issue with the same fixed title:

```
fix: upstream fix for review finding on <repo>#<pr>
```

When one PR review produces several valid findings in files owned by an upstream repository, the upstream repository ends up with many open issues that have the same title. They look like duplicates, but each one is a separate finding. Deduplication by the `aidevops:upstream-route:<repo>#<pr>:<thread_id>` body marker works as intended.

Observed: one downstream PR review routed 18 distinct review threads to a public upstream repository (wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding, issues #802 to #822). All 18 issues have the same title. Each has a different thread ID, file and defect. The maintainer asked "what's with all these duplicate issues?"

Side effects:
- People and triage routines that dedupe by title treat these issues as duplicates.
- `framework-issue-helper.sh` and similar title-based duplicate checks would merge them by mistake.
- An issue list gives no hint of which file or defect each issue covers.

## Fix

Make the title specific to the finding and keep it short:

- Add the primary affected file (the first path after `Files:` in the sanitized details) and a short defect phrase (the first clause of `Defect:`, cut to about 60 characters), for example:
  `fix(scripts/shop-release.sh): mktemp failure unchecked in release() (review finding on <repo>#<pr>)`
- If the details cannot be parsed, fall back to the current title and add the review thread ID's short suffix, so titles are still unique.
- Sanitize the derived title the same way as the body text (remove backticks, angle brackets and CR characters).
- Do not change the body marker, the cache file key or the lookup logic.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`

Change the title construction in `cmd_route_upstream`. A small `_prrts_upstream_title` helper is a good place for the parsing. Existing route-upstream tests (find them with `rg -n "route-upstream|route_upstream" .agents/scripts/tests`) may assert the fixed title; update those assertions if so.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` reports nothing.
- Run the existing route-upstream tests with `PRRTS_UPSTREAM_ISSUE_HELPER` stubbed. Two different threads on the same PR now produce two different titles. The same thread run twice still reuses the issue found by its marker, and no second issue is created.
- A details file without `Files:` or `Defect:` lines falls back to the current title with the thread suffix.

title: t19178: feat(pulse): persistent dispatch exclusions reach the AI brief owner instead of a user session
body:
## Task


When a deterministic dispatch filter skips an `auto-dispatch` issue on every pulse cycle for longer than a threshold (default 24h), Pulse queues that issue once into the existing terminal-blocker recovery intake as `intake: persistent_exclusion`. The entry names the filter. The pulse supervisor, already the AI brief owner for that queue, then either repairs the mechanical cause within existing authority or records exactly one decision that names the human input required. Maintainer, approval and permission gates are never bypassed.

## Done when

- [ ] An `auto-dispatch` issue skipped by the consolidated filter or a cross-cycle block for longer than `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_EXCLUSION_ESCALATE_SECONDS` appears exactly once in `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh pending` with `"intake":"persistent_exclusion"` and the filter reason.
- [ ] The entry retires without a GitHub write once the filter stops skipping the issue for longer than the gap, or the issue closes or loses `auto-dispatch`.
- [ ] Negative: maintainer-gate reasons (`permission_grant_unverified`, `needs_maintainer_permissions`, `cost_budget_exceeded`) never produce a `persistent_exclusion` entry, and the dispatch filters' accept/reject results are unchanged (existing consolidated-label and failure-reason suites pass unchanged).
- [ ] Negative: the mechanical `rearm` pass never prints or releases a `persistent_exclusion` entry.
- [ ] Changed shell files are ShellCheck-clean, and `_tbr_check_entry` stays under the 100-line function gate.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/dispatch-exclusion-age-helper.sh` — runner-local per-issue exclusion ageing. Model on the stamp-file pattern in `_dispatch_consolidated_attention_stamp_path` / `_dispatch_consolidated_attention_fresh` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1526-1545`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:1668-1672` — in `_dispatch_filter_consolidated_candidates`, note each skipped issue with reason `consolidated`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:1724-1738` — in `_dispatch_max_prefilter_cached_block`, note `cross_cycle_<reason>` (sanitized to `[a-z_]+`). Skip maintainer-gate reasons other than `consolidated` (`_dispatch_maintainer_gate_reason`, `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:286-292`); those already surface through `/decisions`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:315-318` — accept `persistent_exclusion` in the `tbr_enqueue` intake case.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:1506-1508` — keep `persistent_exclusion` out of the mechanical `rearm` pass, as with `unclassified_hold`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:1521-1528` — route `persistent_exclusion` to a new checker in `terminal-blocker-recovery-holds.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-holds.sh` — add `_tbr_check_exclusion_entry`, modeled on `_tbr_check_unclassified_entry` (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:1420-1442`). Put it here so the 2024-line helper does not grow.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:513` — add one sentence for the `persistent_exclusion` intake to the terminal-blocker supervisor prompt.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-integration-recovery.md:121` — add a short "Persistent dispatch exclusions" paragraph under "Terminal-blocker recovery".

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pending` / `pending --count` in `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`, consumed by `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` (`pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh:173-226`), which triggers the supervisor; supervisor prompt `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:513`. `record` decisions use the existing `_tbr_decision_active`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the new helper writes only `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-exclusion-age/<owner>--<repo>--<issue>` and calls `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh enqueue ... persistent_exclusion` once per (issue, reason) streak. No GitHub writes in the helper; the supervisor writes through existing guarded helpers only.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-consolidated-label.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` (cross-cycle block lines), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-discovery.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit-lifecycle.sh`. Run them unchanged; add coverage only where a required gate demands it.
- **Schemas/config:** queue entry JSON `{repo, issue, reason, opened_at, intake}` (`tbr_enqueue`, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:323-326`) gains one intake value; no schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copies under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` refresh through `setup.sh` / `aidevops update`; nothing generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A with evidence: `rg -n "dispatch-exclusion-age" .agents/` finds no existing producer or reader, and the queue JSON gains only a new `intake` value that `tbr_enqueue` already stores verbatim, so there is no persisted data to migrate. Ordering: stamps start empty on deploy and accumulate per cycle, so the first escalation lands one threshold (default 24h) after deploy; no backfill is needed because currently stuck issues re-enter through the same per-cycle call sites.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; leftover age stamps are inert files. Queue entries with an unknown intake fall back to `local` (`tbr_enqueue` case default), so retire them by deleting entries with `intake == persistent_exclusion` under `${AIDEVOPS_BLOCKER_RECOVERY_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery}/queue/` (`TBR_ROOT`, `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh:86`), or let `_tbr_check_entry` retire closed issues.

### Implementation Steps

1. Create `dispatch-exclusion-age-helper.sh` with `note <repo> <issue> <reason>` and `active <repo> <issue>`. The stamp holds `first_seen last_seen reason enqueued_reason`. If the reason matches and `now - last_seen` ≤ `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_EXCLUSION_GAP_SECONDS` (default 21600), only `last_seen` advances; otherwise the streak restarts. Once `last_seen - first_seen` ≥ `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_EXCLUSION_ESCALATE_SECONDS` (default 86400; 0 disables) and `enqueued_reason` differs, call `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh enqueue <repo> <issue> <reason> persistent_exclusion` and store `enqueued_reason`. `active` returns 0 while `now - last_seen` ≤ gap. No network calls. Every failure returns 0 to the caller (best-effort, like the attention stamp).
2. Wire the two call sites (steps above). Source nothing new; invoke via `bash "${_PULSE_DISPATCH_LIB_DIR}/dispatch-exclusion-age-helper.sh" note ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` (or an equivalent sourced function). Keep each site to two or three lines so the surgical large-file exemption applies to the 2404-line `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`.
3. Add `_tbr_check_exclusion_entry`. Retire (delete the entry and its decision) when `dispatch-exclusion-age-helper.sh active` fails (the filter stopped skipping it) or the issue lacks `auto-dispatch`. Otherwise apply `_tbr_decision_active` and `_tbr_print_entry ... persistent_exclusion` with public evidence only.
4. Prompt sentence (step 8 file): for `persistent_exclusion`, verify the named filter's cause on current issue/PR evidence. Repair a mechanical defect within existing authority: a stale lifecycle label, a superseded hold, a stale claim with no live owner, or a blocking dependency that is itself stuck (repair or dispatch that dependency). Otherwise post one decision packet naming the exact human input. Never grant permissions or approvals, and record exactly one decision per entry.
5. Run `shellcheck` on every changed shell file and the focused tests below. Then make a WIP commit before broad gates.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** parallel dispatch rounds (t19116) may note the same issue concurrently. Write the stamp via `mktemp` + `mv -f` as `_dispatch_negative_cache_record` does (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:554-568`). A lost update only delays escalation by one cycle.
- **Migration/rollback:** additive; behaviour before the threshold is unchanged. Rollback leaves inert stamps.

title: t19179: fix(pulse): release orphaned active-status labels with no assignee and resurface aged no-auto-dispatch holds daily
body:
## Task


Two additions to existing pulse passes. Both are bounded and run daily in effect.

1. **Orphaned active-status repair (mutating, safe).** Some open issues carry an active ownership status (`status:claimed`, `status:in-review`, `status:in-progress` or `status:queued`) with **zero assignees**, show no activity for `ORPHAN_STATUS_RELEASE_HOURS` (default 24), and have no open linked PR. Post a `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=orphaned_status_no_assignee` audit comment on each, then move it to `status:available` through `set_issue_status`. Never touch `no-auto-dispatch`, `hold-for-review`, `needs-*`, `parent-task` or tier labels, so a held issue stays held.
2. **Aged human-hold resurfacing (read-only).** Widen the supervisor health issue's aged-hold section to cover open issues held by `no-auto-dispatch` or `needs-maintainer-input`, not only `hold-for-review`. Where cheap evidence exists, show a reconsideration hint for each row: "all native sub-issues closed", "a linked PR merged after the hold was applied", or "no activity for N days". Surfacing grants nothing, and the hold stays until a maintainer decides.

## Done when

- [ ] An open issue with `status:claimed` (or in-review/in-progress/queued), zero assignees, idle beyond 24h and no open linked PR receives a `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=orphaned_status_no_assignee` comment, then `status:available`, on the next normalization pass. `no-auto-dispatch` and other hold labels remain.
- [ ] Negative guarantee: no label write happens when an assignee is present, an open linked PR exists, the issue is updated within the threshold, the PR lookup is indeterminate, or the audit comment fails.
- [ ] The supervisor health issue lists aged `no-auto-dispatch` and `needs-maintainer-input` holds alongside `hold-for-review`, deduped and bounded to 10 rows, with a reconsideration hint where available. It never edits labels.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean on both changed scripts.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Worker Quick-Start

1. Read `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh` end to end. Rows come from `_fetch_label_invariant_rows` (lines 304-350); per-issue repairs look like `_enforce_blocked_companion_one_issue` (lines 245-300), which re-reads live labels before writing.
2. Read `_normalize_stale_post_release` and `_normalize_stale_open_pr_blocks_reset` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh` (lines 90-108 and 356-411). Call them; don't copy them. Guard with `declare -F` as this file already does for other cross-file helpers.
3. Read `_health_aged_hold_section` and `_health_hold_recommendation` in `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh:1094-1155`.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh`. Add `assignee_count` and `updated_at` epoch fields to the `_fetch_label_invariant_rows` row; check that the shared `_normalize_repo_listing` payload includes `assignees` and `updatedAt`, and add them to the fallback `--json` field list. Add `_enforce_orphan_active_status_one_issue`, which:
  - re-reads the live issue (state, labels, assignees, updated_at) and requires open, an active core status, and zero assignees;
  - requires idle longer than `ORPHAN_STATUS_RELEASE_HOURS` (integer, default 24, minimum 1);
  - fails closed when `_normalize_stale_open_pr_blocks_reset` reports an open linked PR or is unavailable;
  - persists the `CLAIM_RELEASED` audit through `_normalize_stale_post_release` before any label write, and skips if that fails;
  - then calls `set_issue_status <n> <slug> available`.

  Also add a counter to the summary log line.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh`. In `_health_aged_hold_section`, fetch each label in `HEALTH_HOLD_LABELS` (default `hold-for-review no-auto-dispatch needs-maintainer-input`) separately and dedupe by issue number. Age is measured from the latest `labeled` event for the hold label when available, falling back to `created_at`. Add a `Why reconsider` column, filled by a bounded helper that checks native sub-issues (`repos/{slug}/issues/{n}/sub_issues`: all closed) and the last update age. Keep the 10-row bound, sanitization and read-only contract.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh`. Add a focused case to the existing stubbed-`gh` harness: orphaned `status:claimed`, zero assignees and idle beyond the threshold → audit posted, then `status:available`. Add negative cases: an assignee present, an open linked PR, idle under the threshold, or an audit-post failure → no label write. `no-auto-dispatch` must be preserved.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Never release when the audit comment fails. This matches the GH#35218 rule that a claim is never released silently.
- Do not remove or alter human-hold labels. Resurfacing is read-only.
- Bash 3.2 compatible. Keep existing functions under the complexity gates; add new small helpers instead of growing `_normalize_label_invariants_for_repo`.
- Budget: the orphan check uses the already-fetched listing as a hint and makes one live `gh api` read per candidate only. The dashboard makes at most one sub-issue read per displayed row (10 or fewer).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh`

## Task Brief

## Origin

Interactive session, 2026-11-19. The maintainer asked why #35043 was still unsolved, and then asked: "pulse & workers should have a daily reconsideration of any labels that may have gone stale and preventing an issue from being addressed".

## What

Two additions to existing pulse passes. Both are bounded and run daily in effect.

1. **Orphaned active-status repair (mutating, safe).** Some open issues carry an active ownership status (`status:claimed`, `status:in-review`, `status:in-progress` or `status:queued`) with **zero assignees**, show no activity for `ORPHAN_STATUS_RELEASE_HOURS` (default 24), and have no open linked PR. Post a `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=orphaned_status_no_assignee` audit comment on each, then move it to `status:available` through `set_issue_status`. Never touch `no-auto-dispatch`, `hold-for-review`, `needs-*`, `parent-task` or tier labels, so a held issue stays held.
2. **Aged human-hold resurfacing (read-only).** Widen the supervisor health issue's aged-hold section to cover open issues held by `no-auto-dispatch` or `needs-maintainer-input`, not only `hold-for-review`. Where cheap evidence exists, show a reconsideration hint for each row: "all native sub-issues closed", "a linked PR merged after the hold was applied", or "no activity for N days". Surfacing grants nothing, and the hold stays until a maintainer decides.

## Why

Observed on #35043. The claimer self-unassigned on 2026-11-16 at 20:55Z, but `status:claimed` stayed for three days. Its leaf child #38701 closed on 2026-11-18 through a merged PR, yet nobody reconsidered the parent. A maintainer had to ask and then release it by hand on 2026-11-19.

No current path handles an unassigned active status:

- `_normalize_unassign_stale` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:557-646`) only lists issues **assigned to the runner** with `status:queued`/`status:in-progress` (lines 595-612).
- `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale` Phase 1 reads only **local** claim stamps, and the stamp lives on the claimer's host. Phase 1a requires a self-assignment.
- `release-if-dead` fails closed for cross-host owners and skips `no-auto-dispatch`.
- The label-invariant pass (`.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh:52-97`) enforces status/tier uniqueness and blocked companions, but does not treat "active status + zero assignees" as contradictory.
- #38724 / PR #38725 fixed only the merge-side deadlock this state causes. The issue label itself is still never repaired.

Holds are also never resurfaced. `_health_aged_hold_section` (`.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard-issue.sh:1112-1155`) fetches only `labels=hold-for-review`. On 2026-11-19 this repo had 7 open `no-auto-dispatch` issues, all unassigned, and none appeared on the dashboard. #38861 (macOS qualification, `no-auto-dispatch`, unassigned) is one of them.

Related, but distinct and not to be duplicated: #39327 releases stale **assignees** from `status:available` auto-dispatch issues and edits `pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh`. This task handles the inverse state, an active status with no assignee, and deliberately stays out of that file.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. The design is decided here. The worker extends two existing passes that have reference patterns in the same files.

## Context & Decisions

- "Daily" is met by the 24h idle threshold on the existing per-cycle normalization pass, plus the existing dashboard refresh. No new scheduler or launchd job.
- Releasing to `status:available` is safe because `no-auto-dispatch` still blocks dispatch. A claim is defined as status label plus self-assignment, so a missing assignee means half of the claim is already gone.

title: perf(worktree-cwd): degrade on batch timeout and chunk >4096 PIDs instead of per-PID sudo fallback
body:
## What

Tighten the batched root CWD inspection fallback added in #39333 (for #38918) so a slow or oversized batch does not trigger a long per-PID sudo fallback.

## Why

The #39333 independent security review found no fail-open or disclosure issue. It raised two additive latency findings, and both paths remain fail-closed today:

1. **Batch timeout:** when the batch call times out (caller exit 124 after the 6 s deadline, for example from slow sudo or PAM), `_capture_worktree_proc_cwds_pass` falls back to up to N sequential legacy sudo calls of up to 5 s each.
2. **Oversized request:** with more than `CWDS_MAX_PIDS` (4096) unresolved PIDs, the batch is skipped entirely and the same sequential fallback runs.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` (`_worktree_privileged_read_cwds`): return a distinct status for a timeout (124) versus a refused or unsupported inspector.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-process-providers.sh` (`_capture_worktree_proc_cwds_pass`):
  - On a timeout status, mark every pending link degraded (rc 2) instead of falling back.
  - Keep the per-PID fallback only for a refused or older inspector (one that does not support `--cwds`).
  - Split requests above 4096 PIDs into chunks of 4096 or fewer, applying the same per-chunk validation.
- Pattern: follow the existing strict parser `_worktree_parse_privileged_cwds` and the degraded-visibility contract in `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`. Update that document too.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-process-providers.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`

## Acceptance

- A batch timeout leaves the capture degraded (rc 2) without per-PID sudo calls.
- More than 4096 unresolved PIDs use `ceil(N/4096)` batch calls, and all paths are captured.
- An older inspector without `--cwds` still uses the legacy per-PID fallback.

## Verification

- `/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh` (process cases live in `tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib-process.sh`)
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cwd-inspect.py`
- Docker runtime matrix with real sudo, as described in the #39333 Runtime Testing section
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts

title: security dismiss tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05 dismisses keyv-shaihulud-2026-08 instead
body:
## Observed

`aidevops security dismiss tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05` prints `Dismissed keyv-shaihulud-2026-08`, exits 0, and does not write `tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05` to `~/.aidevops/advisories/dismissed.txt`. The TanStack advisory file stays live and keeps nagging after a clean `aidevops security supply-chain scan`.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/supply-chain-advisory-helper.sh` hardcodes `readonly ADVISORY_ID="keyv-shaihulud-2026-08"` (line 18). `cmd_dismiss` (line 86) always appends that constant and ignores the requested ID. The security CLI appears to route both supply-chain advisory IDs to this helper's `dismiss`.

The TanStack advisory text (`tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05.advisory`) still tells users to run `aidevops security dismiss tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05`, so following the documented step cannot clear it.

## Fix direction

- Make `cmd_dismiss` accept the requested advisory ID, restricted to an allowlist of supply-chain IDs (`keyv-shaihulud-2026-08`, `tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05`). Write that ID and echo it.
- Or, because the keyv IOC pattern already covers the TanStack indicators, retire the TanStack advisory: when the keyv one is dismissed, mark it dismissed too (or delete it on update).
- Files: `.agents/scripts/supply-chain-advisory-helper.sh`, the `aidevops security dismiss` dispatcher, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-supply-chain-advisory-helper.sh`.

## Verification

1. Start from an empty `dismissed.txt`.
2. Run `aidevops security dismiss tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05`. Expect `dismissed.txt` to contain exactly `tanstack-minishaihulud-2026-05`, and the output to name that ID.
3. Run `aidevops security dismiss keyv-shaihulud-2026-08`. Expect it to append only the keyv ID.

**Task ID:** `t19182` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-11-19
**Tags:** `bug` `framework` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(pulse-merge): duplicate PR consolidation stops scoring singleton PRs that cannot form a group

## Done when

- [ ] A backlog with no duplicate linked issue makes zero `_pr_required_checks_pass` calls during consolidation (positive).
- [ ] A backlog with a duplicate worker PR group still scores, selects, verifies, and closes exactly as before: `test-pulse-merge-duplicate-pr-consolidation.sh` passes (negative regression).
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero violations for the edited file.
- [ ] After deploy, the large repo's `deterministic_merge_pass timing` `other_s` falls well below the 64-182 s baseline.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh:273-315`: split `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_groups` into a collect phase and a score phase. The model is the existing six-argument precomputed path in `_pmp_pr_consolidation_health_score` (`pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh:111-151`).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_pmp_prepare_repo_processing_backlog` (`pulse-merge-backlog.sh:762`) is the only production caller and ignores the return value. `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_group` reads the group file in `issue|pr|score|created|draft` format, which stays unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `_pmp_close_superseded_sibling_pr` (unchanged) is the only GitHub write. It runs only for verified multi-PR groups.
- **Schemas/config:** no change. The group-file row format stays the same, and `PULSE_MERGE_CONSOLIDATE_DUPLICATE_PRS` is still honoured.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the deployed copy under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` refreshes through `setup.sh` / `aidevops update`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. The group file is a per-call `mktemp` file, so no persisted state exists.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** to roll back, revert the PR. No persisted state exists to retire. The new candidate temp file is created and removed inside the function, next to the existing group file (`rm -f` before `return 0`). `PULSE_MERGE_CONSOLIDATE_DUPLICATE_PRS=false` remains the runtime kill switch (`pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh:280`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-duplicate-pr-consolidation.sh`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Phase 1: keep the existing TSV loop and worker-owned and linked-issue filters, but write `issue|pr|created|draft|mergeable|review` candidate rows to a temp file without scoring.
2. Phase 2: for each issue listed by `cut -d'|' -f1 | sort | uniq -d`, score each of its candidate rows with `_pmp_pr_consolidation_health_score "$repo_slug" "" "$pr" "$mergeable" "$review" "$draft"` and append `issue|pr|score|created|draft` to the group file.
3. Keep the per-issue `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_group` loop unchanged, and keep `return 0` on every path.
4. Run ShellCheck and the focused test, then make a WIP commit.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** per-call temp files only, so there is no shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** behaviour-preserving. Rows dropped in phase 2 belong to singleton groups, which `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_group` already returns from at `group_count -gt 1`.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** no interface change. The function signature and return value are unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged. Each pass recomputes from the live backlog.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if a temp file cannot be created, fall back to the existing `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` path pattern. Any failure leaves the function a no-op that returns 0.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_groups`, about 43 lines growing to about 60. That is under the 100-line function gate, so no extraction is needed.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-duplicate-pr-consolidation.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck covers the edited script. The consolidation suite proves duplicate groups still score, select, verify and close as before. A read-only profile against the large managed repo proves the singleton backlog makes zero `_pr_required_checks_pass` calls.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required, because there are no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the commands above
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification: not required, the change is scoped

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change candidate selection, the health threshold, issue-label blocks, scope verification, or the close path. Do not change any other merge-pass stage.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive session that filed this task.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-duplicate-pr-consolidation.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Origin

Interactive productivity investigation (session mining of Pulse merge throughput). Found while tracing why CLEAN, APPROVED worker PRs in a large managed repo wait several merge passes.

## What

`_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_groups` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh:273`) runs on every deterministic merge pass. For each worker-owned PR with a linked issue it calls `_pmp_pr_consolidation_health_score`, which calls `_pr_required_checks_pass` (REST check-runs plus required-context and ruleset reads, about 6 s per PR). Only `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_group` uses the score, and it returns at once when an issue has fewer than two PRs. Almost every group is a singleton, so the pass pays for scores it never uses. Score only the PRs whose linked issue has two or more open worker PRs.

## Why

Read-only profile of one large managed repo (`<managed-repo>`, 40-42 open PRs), using the real merge-pass libraries with writes stubbed:

| Stage | Time |
|---|---|
| `_pmp_log_pr_backlog_counts` | 2-3 s |
| `_pmp_sort_prs_by_backlog_priority` | 4.4 s |
| `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_groups`, cold PR-view cache | 104-148 s |
| `_pmp_consolidate_duplicate_pr_groups`, warm PR-view cache (pulse default) | 69 s |
| one `_pr_required_checks_pass` | 5.9 s |
| one `_extract_linked_issue`, warm | 1.5 s |

Each run scored ten PRs, and none of them belonged to a duplicate group. Live `deterministic_merge_pass timing` rows for that repo show `other_s=64-182` (unattributed, which is where this call runs), `total_s=185-425`, and `merged=0` or `1` per pass. The repo slice is gone before a second PR is evaluated. The log has no `Duplicate PR consolidation` decision lines, and the last superseded close in that repo was on 2026-10-12. Meanwhile 6-13 merge-ready PRs wait several passes each. One CLEAN, APPROVED worker PR went green at 22:15Z, but the cursor had already passed it and it stayed unmerged.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: one function in one file, with an existing test suite and a clear equivalence argument.

## Context & Decisions

- Two other options were rejected for this task. Batching PR bodies through one REST pulls read would save the remaining body reads, but it changes the read path. Running consolidation only once per walk changes when duplicates are detected. Scoring only duplicated groups removes about 85% of the warm-cache cost and leaves outcomes unchanged.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-duplicate-consolidation.sh:111-151,211-315`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh:754-766`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:623-638`

## Dependencies

None.

```bash

# authenticates from. Mirrors oauth-pool-helper.sh:37 (V1) and the generated
# V2 shim (setup/modules/tool-install.sh:1061,1074).

		printf '%s\n' "${AIDEVOPS_OAUTH_POOL_FILE:-${HOME}/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json}"
	fi
	return 0
}

# oauth_pool_has_usable_account PROVIDER POOL_FILE: exit 0 when the pool holds
# at least one runnable account. Allowlist (matches provider-auth-pool.mjs:59-64
# plus expired rate-limit normalisation): status missing/active/idle with no
# active cooldown, or rate-limited whose cooldown has expired. Everything else
# (auth-error, billing-error, unknown) is not runnable. Missing file, missing
# jq, malformed JSON or a non-array provider entry return 1. Never prints
# credential material.
oauth_pool_has_usable_account() {
	local provider="$1"
	local pool_file="$2"
	# jq body: map(select(status in allowlist and cooldownUntil <= now)) | length > 0
	return 1
}
```

   Use `aidevops_opencode_profile_id` (`shared-constants.sh:247`) as the profile resolver. Do not read `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE` directly; #39276 is moving headless code onto the profile document.

Then return `oauth_pool_has_usable_account "$provider" "$pool_file"`. In `resolve_api_key`, run Source 5 only when `${HOME}/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` does not exist.

title: t19184: commit-and-pr: 60s push timeout is shorter than normal pre-push hook runtime (~74s), falsely reports a stall
body:
## Task


`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` kills `git push` after a hardcoded 60s (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:1011`, `local push_timeout=60`). On ordinary code diffs the managed pre-push hooks now legitimately take longer than that, so the helper reports a false "pre-push hook stalling" failure and advises `--skip-hooks` / `--no-verify`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` kills `git push` after a hardcoded 60s (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:1011`, `local push_timeout=60`). On ordinary code diffs the managed pre-push hooks now legitimately take longer than that, so the helper reports a false "pre-push hook stalling" failure and advises `--skip-hooks` / `--no-verify`.

## Why

Observed 2026-11-20 on GH#39350 (one-file `aidevops.sh` diff): `commit-and-pr` failed with `Push timed out after 60s` right after `[repo-verify][OK] typecheck passed`. Running the same push manually with hooks enabled succeeded in about 74s. The hooks ran privacy-guard, complexity-guard (3 parallel metrics), repo-verify `bun run typecheck`, then the pre-push quality validation (secretlint + SonarCloud issue count), and all passed. Nothing was stalled.

The comment at lines 1005-1010 still assumes hooks normally finish well under 60s ("the 60s timeout is a safety net for edge cases, not a normal code path"). The repo-verify typecheck added since then made a >60s push the normal case for code diffs. The false advisory steers agents toward `--skip-hooks`, which bypasses real gates. `claim-task-id.sh` already separates local validation budget from transport budget (GH#29417) for this reason.

## How

File: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`, push block around lines 1003-1035.

1. Make the timeout configurable and raise the default above the observed hook runtime, e.g. `local push_timeout="${AIDEVOPS_PUSH_TIMEOUT_S:-300}"`. Validate it as a positive integer and fall back to the default otherwise.
2. Update the comment at 1005-1010 to describe the current hook set and why the default sits where it does.
3. Optional, preferred if cheap: follow the GH#29417 pattern from `claim-task-id-counter.sh`. Run the pre-push validation once under its own budget, then push the transport with `--no-verify` under a short network budget. Report a validation timeout as a validation failure, not a stall.
4. Keep the timeout advisory, but drop the `--no-verify` / `--skip-hooks` suggestion unless the diff is doc-only.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh
- .agents/reference/pre-push-guards.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- A code-diff `commit-and-pr` whose hooks take 60-120s pushes successfully with the default settings.
- `AIDEVOPS_PUSH_TIMEOUT_S=5` still produces the timeout advisory, so the hang detection still works.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` is clean, and `affected-tests-helper.sh run --base origin/main --compare-base` shows no regressions.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:1003-1035`: push timeout and advisory
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`: GH#29417 split between validation and transport budgets (reference pattern)
- `.agents/reference/pre-push-guards.md`: diagnosis guidance that the advisory points to

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

Document the Higgsfield MCP (subscription-credit route) and Higgsfield GPU boxes as a Blender render backend, using evidence from the live trial on 2026-11-19.

## Why

Higgsfield's MCP (`https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp`, OAuth) bills the web subscription credits, not the separate platform API, and exposes scriptable GPU rental (`gpu_rent` / `gpu_rental_exec` / `gpu_rental_stop`). Current docs only cover the platform API and the Playwright UI automator.

- 120-frame 1920x1080 Cycles OptiX 128-sample sunflower scene on 1x L40S: Blender 5.3.0 verified in 34 s, ~4.1 s/frame warm, box lifetime 13 min 17 s, 15.72 credits; frames hash-verified locally; PSNR 88.7 dB vs the Runpod A40 render of the same frame.
- Runpod A40 secure, same scene (2026-11-17): 8.1 s/frame, $0.21.
- Kling 3.0 Turbo 5 s 720p image-to-video from a Blender frame: 7.5 credits, ~80 s.

title: t19187: Qualify SRT proxy resolved-address, redirect and protocol bypass handling
body:
## Task


Add synthetic, offline evidence for:

1. Allowed hostname resolving to a private (RFC 1918), loopback, link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10) or IPv4-mapped IPv6 address: the proxy refuses it.
2. An HTTP redirect from the allowed host to a different host: the client's follow-up request is refused by the proxy.
3. SOCKS / CONNECT to the allowed hostname on a non-443 port, and a raw non-TLS protocol on 443: refused, or the documented behaviour is recorded.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

GH#35043 "Still required" (`.agents/reference/worker-egress-srt.md`, "Before promotion"). The backend allows one exact provider hostname and relies on SRT's host-side proxy plus `deniedResolvedAddresses` (`settings()` in `backend.mjs`: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, fc00::/7) to stop an allowed name from reaching private space. Current canaries prove only that a *different* hostname gets 403. Nothing has tested what happens when the *allowed* name resolves to a private or loopback address, follows a redirect to another host, or is used with non-HTTP(S) protocols through the SOCKS path.

## What

Add synthetic, offline evidence for:

1. Allowed hostname resolving to a private (RFC 1918), loopback, link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10) or IPv4-mapped IPv6 address: the proxy refuses it.
2. An HTTP redirect from the allowed host to a different host: the client's follow-up request is refused by the proxy.
3. SOCKS / CONNECT to the allowed hostname on a non-443 port, and a raw non-TLS protocol on 443: refused, or the documented behaviour is recorded.

## How

- **No external DNS or network contact.** First inspect `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime/dist` (pinned 0.0.83) for how the host proxy resolves names, and look for an injectable lookup or resolver hook. If one exists, drive it from the test with a fixture mapping an allowed test hostname to the target addresses, with owned listeners on those addresses as positive controls.
- If no hook exists and the only route is external DNS or editing `/etc/hosts`, **stop**. Post a decision-ready comment on this issue with the options (for example a wildcard-DNS service, a local resolver, or an upstream SRT change) and their trade-offs. Do not edit host files.
- Note that `link-local` and `169.254.0.0/16` are absent from `deniedResolvedAddresses`. Confirm whether SRT denies them by default; if not, add them in `settings()`, and cover them with the policy unit test.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worker-egress-srt/backend.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/worker-egress-srt.md`

<!-- aidevops:brief-owner-section id=scope-recovery-1 -->
**Scope recovery (worker, evidence):** the commit validator maps changed Node files to the nearest package and requires a package-level `test` script, so `.agents/scripts/worker-egress-srt/package.json` is also edited (one `test` script running the existing `tests/test-worker-egress-srt.mjs`). No other path is added.
<!-- /aidevops:brief-owner-section -->
## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three cases has a recorded result from a real run on Linux or macOS arm64, with positive host controls (positive).
- [ ] Any address class found reachable through the allowed name is added to the denial list, and the unit test asserts it (negative/regression).
- [ ] The doc's "Still required" list is updated.

## Context & Decisions

Synthetic only. Uses the existing provider policy (`network-tier-helper.sh export-provider-policy`); do not create a parallel allowlist.

title: t19190: Design the provider credential boundary and extraction-role envelope for SRT inference
body:
## Task


Produce a decision-ready design, not an implementation, covering:

1. **Credential boundary.** How a provider API key reaches the model client inside the sandbox without it being readable by the workload's tools, written to output, or exfiltrated to the allowed host in an unexpected form. Options to weigh include host-side header injection in a proxy, a short-lived scoped key, and a file descriptor passed at exec time. State which existing aidevops secret paths (`aidevops secret`, gopass) supply it.
2. **Extraction-role envelope.** Which runtime and model client runs inside the sandbox, with what tools disabled, and how `model-replay-runtime.mjs` / `headless-runtime-launch.sh` would invoke the backend in `required` mode, never `auto`.
3. **Filesystem composition review.** An independent review of the read/write envelope for a real extraction case: inputs, evaluator material, sibling cases and executable closures. The doc lists this as still required.
4. **Separate operator decisions** to list, not make: model and settings, wall-time, resource and cost limits, input release, comparison-attempt approval.

body:
## Task


Treat repository paths of the form `todo/research/<task-id>-<slug>.<ext>` as valid path grammar in `task_identity_first_malformed_candidate`, the way `todo/tasks/<task-id>-brief.md` is already exempt.

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

Treat repository paths of the form `todo/research/<task-id>-<slug>.<ext>` as valid path grammar in `task_identity_first_malformed_candidate`, the way `todo/tasks/<task-id>-brief.md` is already exempt.

## Why

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` writes a "Files Changed" list into the PR body. Any PR that edits a task-named research note (for example `todo/research/t19048-remote-3d-render-backends.md`) then fails the Task-ID Collision Guard CI check with `malformed task identity token 't19048-remote-3d-render-backends.md' in PR body`, although the PR title, linked issue and claim are valid. Observed on PR #39358 (run 44644556449); the author had to hand-edit the generated PR body to pass.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` `task_identity_first_malformed_candidate`, extend the existing `brief_path_ere` pre-strip (pattern: the `todo/tasks/...-brief\.md` loop) to also strip `todo/research/(${TASK_IDENTITY_TOKEN_ERE})-[[:alnum:]._-]+` paths, still validating the embedded ID and failing closed when it is invalid.
- Keep arbitrary `<task-id>-suffix` tokens outside these path prefixes malformed.

### Integration recovery

Evidence: `_blocked_by_extract_tids` passes structured `blocked-by` values to task-ID extraction. Excluding research paths from extraction prevents filename IDs from becoming task references, but without a caller guard a path-only blocker could disappear.

Decision: research paths are file locations, not dependency references; preserve fail-closed behavior by treating a research path in a `blocked-by` value as ambiguous. The reducer already marks the unchanged prose-led path as malformed; the shell path must emit the same sentinel.

title: t19192: fix(release): release commands retire their own control and verifier trees at exit instead of leaking them to the next run
body:
## Task


Each non-readonly `aidevops release` command creates `aidevops-release-control-<pid>`. Reconcile also creates `aidevops-release-control-verifier-<pid>`, and both trees are owned by the executor itself (GH#37365, `full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh:32-47`). At exit the trap (`full-loop-release-helper.sh:48-63`) and the verifier cleanup (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:161-162`) ask the registry to retire those trees. The registry answers `waiting-for-runs` / `waiting-for-caller`, because the only live run is the caller's own. The release path never opts in to `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1` (`worker-lifecycle-state.sh:127`). The registry designed that opt-in for this exact case (GH#37432): end the caller's own run, then retry once. As a result, every release command leaks its trees. The next mutating release command reaps them serially in `_full_loop_release_reap_stale_control_worktrees` (`full-loop-release-helper.sh:72-89`). Each reap does a full archive and verification, about 20-50 s per tree, all on the release critical path.

Change: `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree` passes `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1`, so a tree held only by this executor's declared session is retired at exit.

## Done when

- [ ] After a release command exits normally, its own `aidevops-release-control-<pid>` and `aidevops-release-control-verifier-<pid>` trees are gone (positive).
- [ ] Retirement never ends another live session's run: a release tree held by another session is still refused and retained, and the registry tests in `test_enrollment.py` still pass (negative regression).
- [ ] ShellCheck reports zero violations, and both release test suites pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh:49-59`: in `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree`, call `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1 remove_worktree_path_permanently ...`. Model: `worktree-helper-cmds.sh:597`, the explicit-removal path that already opts in.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** every `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree` caller: the EXIT trap (`full-loop-release-helper.sh:54,60`), the stale reaper (`:86`), verifier cleanup (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:140,162`), and the tag and preparation tree removals in `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` and `full-loop-release-helper.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the registry `relinquish-session` (`.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/session.py:71-90`) ends only the run of `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` under `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID`. Both are the executor's own `release:<epoch>:<pid>` identity, and the PID must be an ancestor of the call. Retirement then reruns every preservation check.
- **Schemas/config:** no change. `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER` is an existing call-scoped opt-in (`worker-lifecycle-state.sh:127`), so there is no new config key or schema.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` copy refreshes on `aidevops update`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no persisted state changes. Trees already leaked are still reaped by `_full_loop_release_reap_stale_control_worktrees` (dead PID, 30 min idle).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** to roll back, revert the PR to restore the plain `remove_worktree_path_permanently` call in `full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh`. No state format changes, and refusals keep the tree exactly as today.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh:283-300` (control-tree EXIT cleanup), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reaper.sh`, `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py:834` (explicit removal relinquishes only on waiting-for-caller).

### Implementation Steps

1. In `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree`, prefix the `remove_worktree_path_permanently` call with `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1`. Add a comment that cites GH#37365 (executor-owned trees) and GH#37432 (the relinquish contract).
2. Run ShellCheck and the two release test suites.
3. Runtime check: run one `aidevops release status <recent PR>` and one `aidevops release reconcile <terminal PR>`. Then confirm the trees they created are gone from the worktree base, and that the run no longer ends with `waiting-for-caller`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the registry relinquishes a run only when the runtime PID is this command's ancestor and the session ID matches. A sibling session's or Pulse's run on the same tree is never ended (`session.py:88`, test `test_relinquish_requires_the_caller_runtime`).
- **Migration/rollback:** none. The variable is scoped to the call.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older registries without `relinquish-session` return non-zero. `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_status` then returns 1 and behaviour is unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** relinquish retries at most once (`worker-lifecycle-state.sh:96-100`).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** any refusal keeps the tree. The stale reaper handles it later, as it does today.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree`, 9 lines growing to about 13. No gate impact.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reaper.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** ShellCheck covers the edited library. The release suites cover EXIT-trap and reaper removal. The runtime check covers the live registry relinquish path, which the suites stub.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. This is a scoped change to one release library.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the commands above
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification: not required, the change is scoped

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change registry retirement checks, the preservation archive, the stale-reaper eligibility rules (dead PID, 30 min idle), or `--force` semantics.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive session that filed this task.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-worktree-lib.sh`

</details>

Change: `_full_loop_release_remove_worktree` passes `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_RELINQUISH_CALLER=1`, so a tree held only by this executor's declared session is retired at exit.

## Why

Evidence from one `aidevops release reconcile 39308` run on v3.39.246:

- 22 sequential `{"status":"retired","archive":".../unattributed/<ts>"}` lines between 00:07:30Z and 00:20:52Z, then the release work (about 60 s).
- The run ended with `[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=waiting-for-runs detail=waiting-for-caller rc=0`, which is its own trees being refused at exit.
- Right after the run, 9 trees remained on disk under the worktree base: `aidevops-release-control-<pid>` and 8 `aidevops-release-control-verifier-<pid>`.
- Two `retirement-refused ... database-locked` lines came during the sweep. The long registry write burst also contends with other lifecycle writers. An unrelated bounded operation in the same session was refused with `lifecycle owner admission is unavailable (database-locked)`.

Releases are the close-out step for every merged batch, so this tax lands on every release, reconcile and finalize.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: one function in one library, and it reuses an existing registry contract.

## Context & Decisions

- Two alternatives were rejected. Bounding the stale reaper only moves the cost and lets SIGKILL leaks pile up. Skipping the reaper for reconcile leaves the leak in place. Fixing the leak at its source removes the backlog, and the unchanged reaper stays as the SIGKILL safety net (GH#32528).

title: wp-helper --fluent-boards: add assign/unassign card members
body:
## What happened

An interactive session needed to assign 12 existing Fluent Boards cards to a board member (so the vendor's own AI could find them). `wp-helper.sh --fluent-boards` has no assign action (only `boards | cards | show | add | move | comment | check`), so the session wrote a one-off `wp eval-file` script.

## What worked (pattern to reuse)

Fluent Boards 2.3.0's own bulk path, the same one the board UI uses:

```php
( new \FluentBoards\App\Services\TaskService() )->bulkActions(
    $card_ids, 'assign_members', array( 'user_ids' => array( $user_id ) ), $board_id
);
```

- It only assigns users who are already board members (`BoardService::isAlreadyMember`), skips existing assignees, adds them as watchers, and returns `successful_tasks` / `failed_tasks` / `message`.
- Run as a named admin (`--user=<id>`), like the helper's other writes.
- Removing an assignee: `Task::addOrRemoveAssignee($user_id)` toggles (detaches assignee and watcher if present).

## Proposed change

Add to `.agents/scripts/wp-fluent-boards-writer.php` (and the help text in `wp-helper.sh` / `wp-helper-fluent-boards.sh`):

- `assign --card ID[,ID...] --member USER_ID` (writes need `--user`), via `bulkActions(..., 'assign_members', ...)`; print before/after assignees per card.
- `unassign --card ID[,ID...] --member USER_ID`, via `addOrRemoveAssignee` only when currently assigned.
- `show` / `cards` output: include assignee IDs and names.
- Document in `tools/wordpress/fluent-mcp.md` "Work a setup board".

## Verification

On a test board: assign two cards to a board member, re-run (no duplicates), assign a non-member (refused with the plugin's message), unassign, and check `cards` output shows assignees before/after.

title: fix(pulse-merge): CI-drift update-branch must not fire on policy-gate failures or external crypto-approved PRs
body:
## What

The pulse CI-drift repair (`t2805`) ran `update-branch` on an external, crypto-approved PR whose only terminal required-check failure was the **policy** gate `maintainer-gate`, not CI drift. The new merge commit changed the PR head and invalidated the head-bound maintainer approval signed 90 seconds earlier, so the maintainer had to re-sign. It also re-triggered 20 fork `pull_request` workflows that needed manual approval to run.

## Evidence (PR #39097, external fork, 2026-11-20)

- 00:30:59Z: maintainer signs approval at head `ed9cca98`.
- 00:31:34Z: `pulse-merge.log` shows `process_pr ... #39097 (from approve issue #39095)`.
- Then: `_check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure: 1 terminal failed required context(s)`. That context was `maintainer-gate`, whose last run (23:56Z) failed because the linked issue was briefly unassigned. A gate re-run was already pending from the approval's own PR events.
- Then: `attempting CI-drift rebase via update-branch (t2805)` and `CI-drift rebase succeeded via update-branch` (`pulse-merge.log:662369-662370`). The new head is `be52978a` (`Merge branch 'main' into fix/oc2-oauth-probe`).
- `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 39097` then reported `External/fork PR #39097 has missing cryptographic development authority` and required `sudo aidevops approve batch pr:39097` again.

## Why

- `maintainer-gate` (and `review-bot-gate`) are policy verdicts. Re-running CI on a new base never fixes them, so `update-branch` is the wrong repair.
- For external/fork PRs, the maintainer authority is bound to the exact head (`full-loop-helper-merge-authority.sh:436`). Any pulse-made head change discards the approval it was acting on.
- Fork `pull_request` workflows go to `action_required` on every new head, so CI stalls until a maintainer approves the runs.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` — in the CI-drift rebase function (around `:697-742`, the `t2805` path):
  1. Skip `update-branch` when every terminal failed required context is a policy gate. Use the gate allowlist: `maintainer-gate`, `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`, `review-bot-gate`. Log the reason.
  2. Skip `update-branch` for external/fork PRs (`isCrossRepository` true or the `external-contributor` label). Log that a head change would invalidate the head-bound maintainer approval.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/` — extend the existing CI-drift/update-branch suite (find it with `rg -l 'CI-drift' .agents/scripts/tests`) with the two skip cases.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh
rg -l 'CI-drift' .agents/scripts/tests | xargs -n1 bash
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A PR whose only terminal failed required context is `maintainer-gate` gets no `update-branch`; the log names the policy-gate skip.
- [ ] An external/fork PR never receives a pulse `update-branch` (regression: approval head binding preserved).
- [ ] Internal PRs with a real failed CI context still get the existing CI-drift `update-branch`.

Related: #39097, #39095.
