title: t19194: fix(pulse): orphan interactive PRs with unresolved review threads never reach the review-thread worker
body:
## Task


`_pulse_merge_review_thread_interactive_handover` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:199`) never hands an orphan `origin:interactive` PR (no linked issue) to the review-thread worker. Such a PR is deferred on every merge pass, forever.

`_interactive_pr_is_stale` returns not-stale when the PR has no linked issue unless `allow_orphan=1` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:515-518`). Two other stale paths already recover a tracking issue first: the stale non-draft manual-merge path (`pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:344-348`, GH#23425) and the stale draft path (`_interactive_draft_pr_try_handover`, `pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:379-384`, GH#39158). Both use `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue` (`pulse-merge-process.sh:985`). The review-thread path doesn't. A PR with `allow-auto-merge` passes the policy gate on the label, so it never reaches the recovery at `:344` either.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`_pulse_merge_review_thread_interactive_handover` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:199`) never hands an orphan `origin:interactive` PR (no linked issue) to the review-thread worker. Such a PR is deferred on every merge pass, forever.

`_interactive_pr_is_stale` returns not-stale when the PR has no linked issue unless `allow_orphan=1` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:515-518`). Two other stale paths already recover a tracking issue first: the stale non-draft manual-merge path (`pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:344-348`, GH#23425) and the stale draft path (`_interactive_draft_pr_try_handover`, `pulse-merge-author-checks.sh:379-384`, GH#39158). Both use `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue` (`pulse-merge-process.sh:985`). The review-thread path doesn't. A PR with `allow-auto-merge` passes the policy gate on the label, so it never reaches the recovery at `:344` either.

## Evidence (pulse.log, 2026-11-19 → 2026-11-20)

- `marcusquinn/cloudron-warmbly-app#19` and `marcusquinn/cloudron-orbit-app#10` (`chore: resync framework workflow to aidevops canonical caller`, opened 2026-11-19T04:10Z, labels `origin:interactive,allow-auto-merge`, no linked issue, 1 and 3 unresolved CodeRabbit threads). Every merge pass logs `review-thread remediation deferred ... origin:interactive PR still owned by an active or unverified session after unresolved review-bot thread preflight blocker (GH#38291)`.
- Each pass spends 60–110 s per PR on the full gate stack (`review_and_gates`, `pre_merge`, `admin_merge` stages in `deterministic_merge_pass timing`) before reaching the same blocker. Together that is roughly 150–250 s of the ~555 s merge-pass budget, which usually merges 0–1 PRs across all repos.

## How

In `_pulse_merge_review_thread_interactive_handover`, when `_interactive_pr_is_stale` returns 1, mirror `_interactive_draft_pr_try_handover`: if `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue` is defined and succeeds, re-run `_interactive_pr_is_stale`; hand over only if that now passes. Keep every existing guard. Recovery already enforces collaborator authorship (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`), the `no-takeover`/`hold-for-review`/`needs-maintainer-review`/`external-contributor` opt-outs, the 12 h orphan age floor and enforce mode. Fresh or claimed PRs still defer.

## Files

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`: `_pulse_merge_review_thread_interactive_handover` (~line 199-216). The handover cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh` (~line 420-480) stub `_interactive_pr_is_stale`/`_interactive_pr_trigger_handover`. Add one case with `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue` stubbed: orphan becomes stale after recovery and hands over. Add one case where recovery fails and the PR still defers.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-review-thread-remediation.sh` passes, plus `test-pulse-merge-interactive-handover.sh` and `test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-unbound-var-check.sh` are clean.
- After deploy, the next merge pass over the two PRs above logs a tracking issue (`Track interactive PR #N`) and an `origin:worker-takeover` handover instead of the deferral line.

## Follow-up (not in scope)

The deferral itself is not memoised, so even a genuinely owned interactive PR re-runs the 60–110 s gate stack every pass at an unchanged head. A head+thread-fingerprint memo with a TTL (like the GH#38259 parked-head skip) is a separate task.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: t19195: fix(dependency-reconciler): external_trigger_pending holds are released on closed native edges because the release's own needs-dependency label supersedes them
body:
## Task


`dependency-event-reconciler.sh` releases `external_trigger_pending` holds as soon as the issue's native blocked-by edges are closed, even when the trigger the worker named (an event date, an open non-native issue, unfinished sibling rows) has not happened. Each release re-arms a full worker, which re-reads live state, reports "nothing has changed since the last attempt" and releases blocked again. This repeats on every runner in the fleet.

Root cause is the GH#38866 supersession rule in `_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:490-507`). It strips terminal-blocker lines from every trusted comment older than the latest `labeled needs-dependency` event, treating that label as a later recovery decision. But `needs-dependency` is also the companion the worker release itself applies for `external_trigger_pending` (`blocked_needs_label_for_reason`, `shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:662`; companion line in `_terminal_blocker_recovery`, `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:1179-1188`). The release posts the observation and labels it roughly 10-15 s later, so every fresh observation, and the `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` comment, is immediately "superseded". `_der_has_hold` then sees no hold, `_der_native_blockers_closed` passes, and `_der_try_unblock` (`:509-562`) removes `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` and adds `status:available`.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`dependency-event-reconciler.sh` releases `external_trigger_pending` holds as soon as the issue's native blocked-by edges are closed, even when the trigger the worker named (an event date, an open non-native issue, unfinished sibling rows) has not happened. Each release re-arms a full worker, which re-reads live state, reports "nothing has changed since the last attempt" and releases blocked again. This repeats on every runner in the fleet.

Root cause is the GH#38866 supersession rule in `_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:490-507`). It strips terminal-blocker lines from every trusted comment older than the latest `labeled needs-dependency` event, treating that label as a later recovery decision. But `needs-dependency` is also the companion the worker release itself applies for `external_trigger_pending` (`blocked_needs_label_for_reason`, `shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:662`; companion line in `_terminal_blocker_recovery`, `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:1179-1188`). The release posts the observation and labels it roughly 10-15 s later, so every fresh observation, and the `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` comment, is immediately "superseded". `_der_has_hold` then sees no hold, `_der_native_blockers_closed` passes, and `_der_try_unblock` (`:509-562`) removes `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` and adds `status:available`.

## Evidence (one managed private repo, 24 h window ending 2026-11-20T02:00Z)

- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary`: one repeated blocker fingerprint, reason `external_trigger_pending`, 35 terminal attempts across 31 issues in 24 h. Average worker session is about 22 min, so roughly 13 worker-hours a day.
- Sampled worker reports: "BLOCKED: nothing has changed since the last attempt. Dependency: <issue> is still open" (that issue is not a native edge); "sibling phases closed with unfinished ledger rows"; "the ceremony where winners are announced hasn't happened yet". Three of four sampled issues have native `blockedBy` edges that are all CLOSED (GraphQL `blockedBy { nodes { state } }`), while the named trigger is still pending.
- Timeline pattern on one issue: worker release posts `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` + `Terminal blocker: reason=external_trigger_pending` at T, the same runner labels `needs-dependency` at T+13 s, another fleet runner later removes `status:blocked`/`needs-dependency` and adds `status:available` in one edit, and the next dispatch repeats the same blocker.
- A fourth issue (no native or declared blockers, so not this path) still lost `status:blocked` and then `needs-dependency` as two separate removals 2 s apart with no status added, and no comment, on another fleet runner, after its circuit was `active=true observations=2`. This shape matches a REST-fallback status transition (`_rest_issue_apply_delta_plan` removes first, `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh:749-760`) whose add did not land. Identify that caller as part of this task if it is cheap; otherwise record the finding in the PR and leave it out of scope.

## How

1. In `_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion`, a `needs-dependency` label event must only supersede observations that a later recovery decision converted. Do not count the release's own companion labelling. Options, in preference order: (a) require the cutoff `labeled needs-dependency` event to follow the observation by more than a small window (e.g. 120 s) *and* be preceded by evidence of a recovery decision after the observation (a `blocked_by_added` timeline event or a trusted non-ops recovery comment); (b) never strip `reason=external_trigger_pending` observations or `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` comments, leaving their release to `terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` (GH#38353) or a trusted `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`. Pick the smallest rule that keeps the GH#38866 case working: a `target_code_blocker` observation converted by AI recovery into a native dependency still releases when that dependency closes.
2. Keep every trust boundary (`#aidevops:trust-boundary` comments on `:476`, `:498`, `:521`) and fail-closed behaviour (unreadable events keep every observation).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: `_der_comments_after_dependency_conversion` (~490-507); `_der_try_unblock` (~509-562) only if needed.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: extend the existing GH#38866 supersession cases. Add (i) an `external_trigger_pending` observation whose `needs-dependency` label lands seconds after it, with closed native blockers, which must stay `held`; (ii) the existing GH#38866 converted `target_code_blocker` case, which must still unblock.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`

title: t19196: fix(worker-lifecycle): self-merged worker PRs without MERGE_SUMMARY are recorded as failures; backfill the summary instead
body:
## Task


A worker whose exact-head PR merged with a correct same-repo `Resolves #N` link is still recorded as a failure when the PR has no `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment. The lifecycle probe returns `merged_missing_summary` (`.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:279-289`). `headless-runtime-worker.sh:1708-1713` then marks the session `failed` (`worker_merged_missing_summary`), and the objective-outcome record gets `effective_outcome=failed` with `next_action=narrow_redispatch`. The issue itself is closed as completed (`status:done`, `solved:worker`), so the failure is false.

GH#39205 (t19141, shipped v3.39.241) fixed the pulse-merged form by accepting the `PULSE_MERGE_CLOSEOUT:PR#N` marker. It does not cover PRs that a worker opened and merged itself without going through `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, the only path that posts the summary (`_post_merge_summary`, `full-loop-helper-commit.sh:2066`; called from `full-loop-helper.sh:479`). Some repository briefs tell workers to open their own data PR, so the summary is never posted.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## What

Some repository briefs tell workers to open their own data PR, so the summary is never posted.

## Evidence (24 h ending 2026-11-20T02:00Z, `~/.aidevops/state/objective-evidence.jsonl`)

- 31 `attempt_outcome` records with `raw_result=success`, `classification=worker_merged_missing_summary`, `effective_outcome=failed`: the largest single class of "failed" outcomes. All come from one managed private repo, and they keep occurring after v3.39.241 (the latest at 2026-11-20T00:04Z).

Its only comments are CodeRabbit and a security-scan bot, with no MERGE_SUMMARY and no closeout. The issue is closed with `status:done,solved:worker`.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary` groups these as `ff-v1:other-failure` (52 sessions, `next_action: none`; results `success:42`). False failures also feed the tier cascade: another issue in the same repo shows "Cascade Tier Escalation: tier:standard → tier:thinking, Trigger: 1 consecutive worker failures", which moves work onto a costlier model.

## How

In the `merged_missing_summary` branch of the worker lifecycle (`headless-runtime-worker.sh` ~1708), backfill instead of failing. The probe already verified exact head, merged state and same-repo closing linkage (`_pr_handoff_has_linked_issue` runs before the summary check):

Build the What/Files fields from the PR (`gh api repos/<slug>/pulls/<n>` title and `/files`). Keep its idempotency (skip when a canonical summary exists) and signature footer; never hand-compose the footer.
2. Re-probe with `_pr_handoff_has_merge_summary`. If it is now present, treat the session as the normal `merged` success (`worker_complete` release, `_HRW_TELEMETRY_SUCCESS`). If the backfill or re-probe fails, keep today's failed classification so nothing is silently upgraded.

- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh` already covers `merged_missing_summary`. Add one case: backfill succeeds, then the outcome is success. Add one case: backfill fails, then the outcome stays failed.

title: t19198: fix(pulse-merge): merge-ready resume lane starved by per-repo slice; run merge lane before CI-repair lane and exempt it from the slice
body:
## Task


On large repos the deterministic merge pass merges almost nothing: promoted merge-ready PRs are starved by the per-repo slice. `_pmp_resume_cursor_with_priority_lane` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh:962`) reorders a resumed walk as `resume item → CI-repair lane → merge-ready lane → tail`. The per-repo slice (`_pmp_merge_repo_slice_deadline`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh:337`, one third of the ~555 s pass, so ~185 s) binds after the first processed unit (`_PMP_MERGE_REPO_SLICE_PROGRESS=1`, set by enrichment and by `_pmp_record_processed_pr_result`). Enrichment (~25-70 s) plus one unmergeable resume item (70-115 s) plus a CI-repair item exhaust the slice. The pass pauses, the next resume promotes the same merge-ready PRs behind a new resume item, and they never run.

This contradicts `.agents/workflows/pulse.md` "Priority Order" item 1 (green CI → merge before failing CI → fix). It is why an interactive `/full-loop` that merges its own PR finishes in minutes while the same ready PR waits hours for the pulse.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

On large repos the deterministic merge pass merges almost nothing: promoted merge-ready PRs are starved by the per-repo slice. `_pmp_resume_cursor_with_priority_lane` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-backlog.sh:962`) reorders a resumed walk as `resume item → CI-repair lane → merge-ready lane → tail`. The per-repo slice (`_pmp_merge_repo_slice_deadline`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh:337`, one third of the ~555 s pass, so ~185 s) binds after the first processed unit (`_PMP_MERGE_REPO_SLICE_PROGRESS=1`, set by enrichment and by `_pmp_record_processed_pr_result`). Enrichment (~25-70 s) plus one unmergeable resume item (70-115 s) plus a CI-repair item exhaust the slice. The pass pauses, the next resume promotes the same merge-ready PRs behind a new resume item, and they never run.

This contradicts `.agents/workflows/pulse.md` "Priority Order" item 1 (green CI → merge before failing CI → fix). It is why an interactive `/full-loop` that merges its own PR finishes in minutes while the same ready PR waits hours for the pulse.

## Evidence (2026-11-20, `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`)

- Four consecutive aidevops resumes logged `moved 2 merge-ready PR(s) and 2 CI-repair PR(s) behind resume item`, then `graceful time budget exhausted ... pausing at PR cursor index=N+1`. The cursor advanced 11→12, 13→14 and so on, with `merged=0`.
- Timing rows: `repo=marcusquinn/aidevops total_s=194 ... merged=0 prs=18 enrichment_s=48 pr_s=114 slowest_pr=#39375:114s` and `repo=<large-private-repo> total_s=185 ... merged=0 prs=42 slowest_pr=...:105s`. A full pass: `total_s=556 merged=0`.
- `PR backlog marcusquinn/aidevops: merge-ready=3..4` on every cycle. A planning PR labelled `allow-auto-merge` stayed CLEAN and unmerged for over 3 hours.

## How

1. In `_pmp_resume_cursor_with_priority_lane`, order the lane as `resume item → merge-ready lane → CI-repair lane → tail` (swap `$ci` and `$lane` in the jq reorder at ~1003-1007). Lane bounds `_PMP_RESUME_LANE_START/END` stay the same, so `_pmp_lane_clamped_cursor` and `_pmp_pause_merge_pr_cursor` are unchanged. Record the merge-lane end index (`_PMP_RESUME_MERGE_LANE_END = LANE_START + merge_moved`).
2. Exempt only merge-lane items from the per-repo slice: the loop in `_merge_ready_prs_for_repo` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:445-472`) sets a dynamically scoped `_PMP_MERGE_LANE_SLICE_EXEMPT=1` while the index is inside the merge lane. `_pmp_merge_effective_deadline_epoch` (`pulse-merge-pass.sh:291`) ignores the slice when the flag is set. The whole-pass deadline, stop flag, cooldown and REST-core checks still bind, and every gate still runs.
3. Keep the resume item first (the GH#39281 progress guarantee). The exemption stays bounded: `PULSE_MERGE_RESUME_PRIORITY_LIMIT` (default 2, guardrail 10), plus `_pmp_lane_already_served`, which promotes each head at most once.

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`

title: fix(dependency-reconciler): brief-template 'Action required: None' falsely matches ACTION REQUIRED hold (case-insensitive grep)
body:
## What

`dependency-event-reconciler.sh` treats the brief-template line `- **Action required:** None.` as the supervisor's `ACTION REQUIRED` human-hold marker. As a result, dependency-blocked issues whose brief has a Complexity Impact section stay `status:blocked` + `needs-dependency` after every blocker closes.

## Evidence (2026-11-20)

- #39352 (t19183) was blocked only by #39095. #39095 closed when PR #39097 merged (`a647d8db`).
- Reconciler output: `[dependency-reconciler] closure repo=marcusquinn/aidevops closed=#39095 dependants=1 unblocked=0 not_ready=0 held=1`.
- #39352 has no hold label and no hold comment. The body's Complexity Impact section has `- **Action required:** None.`, generated from `.agents/templates/brief-template.md:381`.
- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:118` puts `ACTION REQUIRED` in `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE`, and `:127` matches it with `grep -qiE`, which ignores case.
- The other consumers of the same supervisor marker match case-sensitively: `pulse-dep-graph.sh:508` (`grep -E`), `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1639` (`grep -F 'ACTION REQUIRED'`), and `pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh:42`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:124-134` (`_der_text_has_strong_hold`): match the machine markers in `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE` (`HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED`, `ACTION REQUIRED`, `aidevops:brief-hold`, `Worker Watchdog Kill`) case-sensitively, the same way `pulse-dep-graph.sh:508` does. If `worker[_ -]blocked` really needs case-insensitive matching, keep it in its own `-i` check.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial.sh` (or the closest reconciler test, found with `rg -l '_der_text_has_strong_hold' .agents/scripts/tests`): add two cases. A body with `- **Action required:** None.` is not held. A comment with `ACTION REQUIRED: refresh token` is still held.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler-partial.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dependency-blocked issue whose body contains `**Action required:** None.` is unblocked when its last blocker closes.
- [ ] Supervisor `ACTION REQUIRED` comments, `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED`, and `aidevops:brief-hold` still hold the issue.

title: t19199: fix(worker-lifecycle): treat a linked, merged worker PR without MERGE_SUMMARY as completion when its issue is closed
body:
## Task


Treat a worker's exact-head, merged, same-repo-linked PR as completion when its issue is closed, even with no `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment. Today that state (`merged_missing_summary`) is the largest false-failure class: the issue is closed `status:done`/`solved:worker`, yet the session is recorded `failed` (`worker_merged_missing_summary`), the outcome becomes `narrow_redispatch`, and the tier cascade can escalate later work to a costlier model.

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

It is still the largest failed class after v3.39.241 (GH#39205 fixed only the pulse-merged closeout-marker form). The latest record is from 2026-11-20 on v3.39.247.

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh` `_hrw_pr_output_class` (~172-176): route `merged_missing_summary` through `_hrw_merged_pr_output_class` like `merged`. title: Pulse dispatch stalls (canary rc=75, provider=unknown) while model-availability cache holds a stale anthropic no-key row despite a usable OAuth pool
body:
## What happened

For about 24 h on a single-user install (aidevops 3.39.247, OpenCode V2 worker profile, Anthropic OAuth only, no API keys), every pulse dispatch was skipped:

```
[dispatch_with_dedup] Skipping #N in <owner>/<repo> — no selectable model in tier standard (every candidate backed off or unavailable); will retry next cycle (GH#38717)
[lifecycle] canary_model_selection_unavailable role=worker tier=standard rc=75
```

The capacity line in each failing cycle said:

```
Dispatch_capacity: ... provider=unknown provider_accounts_total=0 provider_accounts_available=-1 account_cap=-1 ...
```

At the same time:

- `model-availability-helper.sh status` showed `anthropic no-key`. `probe_log` held one earlier row, `anthropic health_probe key_invalid HTTP 401` (a stale static key had been probed once), and no later anthropic probe.
- `model-availability-helper.sh resolve thinking --quiet` returned rc=1 ("configured candidates and extended chain exhausted"), so `PULSE_MODEL` (pulse-wrapper-config.sh:185) was empty.
- Both OAuth pools (interactive and `runtimes/opencode-v2/auth/oauth-pool.json`) held one `active` anthropic account with no cooldown. `headless-runtime-helper.sh select` and `canary --role worker --tier standard` passed when run by hand, including under `env -i` with the launchd plist environment.

## What fixed it

`model-availability-helper.sh check anthropic --force` re-probed, resolved the account through the OAuth-pool source (`oauth-refresh-available`) and recorded `healthy`. In the next pulse cycle the capacity line showed `provider=anthropic provider_accounts_total=1 provider_accounts_available=1`, and three workers dispatched. The pulse's own later re-probe also recorded `healthy`.

## Suspected defect

A `no_key` / `key_invalid` row in `model-availability.db` `provider_health` appears to survive past its TTL, or stops being re-probed, after the static key that produced it has gone. That leaves `resolve` failing and the pulse at `provider=unknown`. It is still unclear how the pulse-level `provider=unknown` state turns into worker canary rc=75: the manual canary never reproduced it. Worth tracing whether the dispatch path passes a pulse-derived tier, provider or allowlist into the canary when `PULSE_MODEL` is empty.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-probe-lib.sh`: `_probe_return_cached`, `_probe_resolve_and_validate_key`, `probe_provider`
- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`: `resolve_api_key` sources 4 and 5 (auth.json, OAuth pool)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh:181-189` (`PULSE_MODEL` resolution)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: `_pulse_capacity_selected_provider`, `_pulse_capacity_fallback_provider`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`: `_dlw_canary_preflight`

## Acceptance

- A stale `no_key` / `key_invalid` health row for a provider whose OAuth pool has a usable account is re-probed (or ignored) within one TTL, without a manual `--force`.
- When `PULSE_MODEL` resolution fails but a worker tier has a selectable model, dispatch is not blocked. The pulse logs an explicit warning naming the stale health row.

## Verification

Seed `provider_health` with `anthropic|no_key` and an old `checked_at`, keep one active anthropic account in the V2 pool and no static key, then run one pulse cycle. Expect `provider=anthropic` in `Dispatch_capacity` and a dispatched worker.

## What

Apply the closed-issue completion rule from t19196 (#39394, PR #39406) to the worker failure-recovery path. `_recover_worker_output_on_failure` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` (~372-403) still sends `merged_missing_summary` to the retained-claim branch (`worker_merged_missing_summary`, failed) without reading the issue state. title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: security fix blocked on stock macOS: Python 3.9 lacks tomllib, Codex TOML marked mcp-unreadable, all fixes skipped
body:
## What

`aidevops security fix` can never apply any fix on a stock macOS install when `~/.codex/config.toml` exists, because the default `python3` (Apple's 3.9.6) has no `tomllib`.

## Observed (aidevops 3.39.247, macOS, OpenCode 1.19.6)

- `python3` resolves only to `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6); there is no Homebrew Python.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_mcp.py` `parse_config()` (~l.75-80) imports `tomllib` for `.toml` paths. On 3.9 it raises `ImportError`, and `mcp_findings()` (~l.91-92) records `mcp-unreadable`.
- `.agents/scripts/credential_audit.py` `fix()` (~l.112-114) treats any `mcp-unreadable` as "Incomplete audit; ... no fixes applied" and returns 1, so every other remediation (perms, links, import, prune, leftovers) is skipped.
- The `aidevops security scan` output reports it as `[HIGH] ~/.codex/config.toml mcp-unreadable` with a generic "aidevops security fix" remediation, which is the very command it blocks. A user who follows the advice gets no guidance on the cause.

Installing a newer Homebrew Python is not a safe general fix: user launchd jobs often run `python3` from a PATH that puts `/opt/homebrew/bin` first, and they depend on packages installed for the system interpreter (here: PyYAML for a daily sync job).

## Suggested fix

One of these (worker to choose):
1. Resolve a Python >= 3.11 interpreter explicitly for the credential audit (e.g. search `python3.13`, `python3.12`, `python3.11`, then the uv-managed Python), and fall back to `python3`.
2. Or, on `ImportError`, fall back to `tomli` if importable. Otherwise emit a distinct category such as `mcp-unreadable-python-too-old` whose remediation names the cause, and do not let that category alone block the unrelated fixes in `fix()`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/credential_mcp.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/credential_audit.py`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/secret-hygiene-helper.sh`

## Verification

On a Python 3.9 interpreter with a valid Codex TOML present, `aidevops security scan` names the Python version as the cause, and `aidevops security fix` still offers the non-TOML fixes.

title: t19202: fix(headless): worker DB init fails exit 86 when shared OpenCode DB is briefly locked
body:
## Task


Stop worker launches from failing with exit 86 ("Worker database could not initialise from the shared OpenCode schema") when the shared OpenCode DB is briefly locked, and stop the worker-side ledger/seed copies from taking the shared DB's write lock.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`, `_initialize_worker_db_from_shared_schema`: retry the whole initialisation a bounded number of times with a short backoff (default 4 attempts, about 30 seconds in total, overridable by environment). Capture the SQLite error text and log `[lifecycle] db_schema_init_retry attempt=N step=<step> detail=<sqlite error>` so a remaining failure names its cause.
2. Same file, `_copy_worker_db_migration_ledger_table` and `_seed_worker_db_session_context`: change `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` to `BEGIN` (deferred). The first statement in each transaction is a `DELETE FROM main...`, so the write lock is taken on the worker DB only and the shared DB is read under a shared lock. `_merge_worker_db` keeps `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` because it writes the shared DB.
3. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`: no behaviour change. It keeps calling the init function and still exits 86 after retries are exhausted.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh` (extend the existing init/ledger cases only; no new harness)

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-database-tests.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop worker launches from failing with exit 86 ("Worker database could not initialise from the shared OpenCode schema") when the shared OpenCode DB is briefly locked, and stop the worker-side ledger/seed copies from taking the shared DB's write lock.

## Why

Pulse worker logs from 2026-11-19/20 show 15 launches that failed with exit 86 at `headless-runtime-invoke.sh` `_invoke_opencode_export_isolation`, against 721 successful `db_schema_initialized` launches. Each failure releases the claim, records `result=local_error` / `launch_failure_cause=local_runtime_error`, and counts as a worker terminal failure in `worker-terminal-health.py` `terminal_counts`. Three or more of those within the observation window halve dispatch capacity (`pulse-capacity.sh`), so a transient SQLite lock costs both the launch and later slots.

Evidence:

- Failures cluster in 20-60 second windows (2026-11-19T23:05:40Z, 23:15:48-52Z, 2026-11-20T02:36:31Z, 03:59:25-04:00:07Z). Each window coincides with a worker exit whose `_merge_worker_db` also failed reading the shared DB: raw `Error: in prepare, database is locked (5)` then `db_merge_failed` (15 merge failures versus 698 `db_merged`).
- Each failed init takes about 6 seconds, which matches the 5 second `.timeout` in `sqlite3_with_timeout`. No ledger warning is printed, so the failing call is one of the shared-DB reads in `_initialize_worker_db_from_shared_schema` (`.schema --nosys` or `PRAGMA user_version`), whose stderr goes to `/dev/null`. The cause stays recorded as `unknown`.
- A local reproduction shows that `ATTACH shared` followed by `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on the worker connection takes the attached shared DB's write lock. While another connection holds a write transaction on the shared DB, it fails after the busy timeout. A deferred `BEGIN` whose first statement writes `main` succeeds immediately. `_copy_worker_db_migration_ledger_table` and `_seed_worker_db_session_context` only write the worker DB, but both use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so they compete with interactive sessions and worker merges for the shared write lock.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a held write transaction on a copy of the shared DB, worker-DB ledger copy and session seeding succeed instead of failing after the busy timeout.
- A transient shared-DB read lock during initialisation produces `db_schema_init_retry` lifecycle lines and then `db_schema_initialized`, not exit 86.
- A persistent failure still returns 1 after the bounded attempts, and the caller still writes exit 86.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh` is clean, and the existing headless-runtime database tests pass.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-database.sh`
- `git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*headless*'`, then run the database and invoke tests found there.
- After deployment, count launch failures: `rg -l "Worker database could not initialise" ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/pulse` should stop growing, and `rg -c db_schema_init_retry` shows retries that recovered.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #31068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #31068

**Parent issue:** #31068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
       - **Quoted directives (GH#38827):** in the inlined sources below, every line-start `requires-secrets:`, `requires-ssh:`, `requires-tools:`, `requires-loopback-health:` and `requires-device:` line is quoted with a `> ` prefix, and every `<!-- aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->` marker is renamed `<!-- quoted-parent-directive aidevops:needs-secrets ... -->`, so this GitHub-only task is not gated on them. Restore each one in the merged spec unquoted (no `> ` prefix, original marker name) at the start of a line, so the successor keeps its runner gate.
    - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #31068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#31068 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 31068 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available` — never the parent's ownership status (`status:queued`, `status:claimed`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review`). Immediately before creating the successor, re-read the parent's labels; if it now carries `status:blocked`, use `status:blocked` instead, because that label records an unresolved dependency or hold rather than ownership. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status, and the pre-claim gate holds a `status:blocked` successor until its blocker is released.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent and verify each handoff.** Run all five commands below for #31068, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing and the state check). Every command must succeed:

```bash
gh issue comment 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 31068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 31068 $NEW_NUM
# Re-read the parent (GH#37600); this must print exactly: closed not_planned
gh api "repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/31068" --jq '.state + " " + (.state_reason // "")'
```

   **Handoff verification (GH#37600):** a parent that still reads `open` keeps the `consolidated` label while the dispatch gate rejects it, so it consumes dispatch attempts every cycle. If any command above fails or refuses the write (for example a worker target-scope guard on a non-target issue), or any parent re-read is not `closed not_planned`, this task has FAILED: do not run step 5 and do not report success. Leave this consolidation task open, record the parent number, the failing command and its output in one comment here, and exit `BLOCKED`. Report a reopen observed after your close as evidence, with its event time; do not guess its cause.

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** only after every parent passed the step 4 verification, with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #31068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #31068.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What
